mappings.note: Pairs the conductivity exceptions on both sides of the classification - LO-1. DEFECT: the stored answer for the metal half reads '[name lost in extraction; the standard answer is mercury, or lead]', so the item ships without a usable key.
Definition of malleability as a physical property of metals - LO-1 vocabulary, not an application or reaction.
Definition of ductility. Same LO-1 basis as the malleability item; the two are honestly identical in curricular demand and differ only in which property is named.
One-word recall for amphoteric oxides and for iodine's lustre - both are property-based classification facts under LO-1.
Equation for one named metal with steam. The product is the demand; no metal is ranked against another, so LO-1 not LO-2.
Carbon dioxide dissolving to carbonic acid is the acidic-oxide behaviour that marks a non-metal - LO-1's chemical-property clause. The high-pressure framing is context only.

POOR FIT. Asks why PVC, a polymer rather than a non-metallic element, is used as insulation; the curriculum has no outcome for materials and their uses. LO-1 cited only for the underlying non-conduction idea. Second instance of this PVC defect in the chapter.

Requires the reason (copper above silver) and the displacement equation - LO-2's predictive clause. The black deposit is displaced silver, not a corrosion product, so LO-7 does not apply despite the wording.
Sorts four oxides into acidic and basic, which is the standard chemical test separating non-metals from metals - LO-1.
Explicit reactivity ordering of four named metals - the first clause of LO-2, with no displacement or extraction asked.
Explains why nitric acid breaks the metal+acid=hydrogen rule. The variable is the acid's oxidising power, not the metals' ranking, so LO-1's chemical-property clause and not LO-2.
Hardness of ionic compounds explained by interionic attraction. No outcome covers compound properties, so the competency, which names compound formation and valency, is the closest legal code.

Explains a single observation about calcium in water via hydrogen bubbles adhering to it. One metal, one reaction, so LO-1; contrast the items that pick calcium out of a list of metals, which are LO-2.
Identifies basic copper carbonate as the corrosion product formed in damp air - LO-7. Near-duplicate of an earlier item, so it honestly takes the same code.
Infers series position from whether a metal occurs free or combined, and demands the reason. The reasoning is pure ranking (LO-2); no ore treatment or extraction step appears, so LO-6 is not cited.
Equation for calcium in water - a single metal's reaction product under LO-1. Duplicated elsewhere in the chapter; the code is the same because the demand is the same.
Equation for steam over red-hot iron. DEFECT: this is a verbatim duplicate of an earlier item in the same chapter, question and answer alike; it shares LO-1 for the same single-metal reason.
Roasting of a sulphide ore to the oxide - a named pre-reduction step in LO-6's extraction sequence, not a general chemical property of zinc.
Explains why ores are converted to oxides before reduction - the rationale for the roasting/calcination stage, squarely LO-6.
Picks two metals out of five by their relative behaviour with boiling water and with steam. Answerable only by ranking the five, so LO-2 and not the single-metal reading of LO-1.
Metal and non-metal identified by liquid state at room temperature. DEFECT: verbatim duplicate of an earlier very-short item in this chapter; same LO-1 demand.
Explains absence of conduction in solid ionic compounds by immobile ions. A compound-structure explanation with no outcome; the competency is the closest legal code.
Asks outright whether X is a metal or a non-metal, judged from a neutral oxide - LO-1's classification demand.

Same copper/silver nitrate set-up as the earlier item but the demand is explicitly which metal is more reactive and why - the ranking clause of LO-2. Two questions on one experiment honestly share the outcome.
Uses of metals traced back to malleability and ductility. The properties are the explanatory core, so LO-1; no outcome covers uses in their own right.
